source: Spiridonov, Erofeeva, Klowait, Morozov, Ardislamov (2025/2026) The modulating role of sources of difficulty in interactive matchstick algebra
finding: Failed conceptual replication (3 experiments) of the claim that physical interaction raises matchstick solve rates. The Knoblich 1999 difficulty order held: A easiest, then B, D, with C (tautology) hardest. Interactivity did not help overall.
numbers: Exp1 interactive assembled sticks N=54 vs static sticks N=51: A .91/.94, B .87/.80, C .59/.59, D .67/.69. Exp3 VR: interactive sticks N=24 A 1.0, B .92, C .62, D .96; VR assembled N=21 B .76, C .67, D .81; static VR N=28 B .86, C .57, D .82. Bayesian logistic regression: only VR interactive sticks credible (+0.67 log-odds [0.22,1.15], about 92%, +6pp). Problem B -1.59, C -2.95, D -1.93 log-odds (CIs exclude 0). Total movements -0.015 [-0.042,0.014]. 5-min vs 3-min +0.27 [0.16,0.38].
quote: failed to reproduce interactive solutions amongst our participants
limits: Baseline accuracy about 86 percent, far above Knoblich 1999 rates, so ceiling effects are likely. Small cells (20-28) in Exp2 and Exp3. Russian university students, between-subjects, one set of four problem types.
agent_relevance: Confirms the item difficulty order behind RCT-style triggers and shows that acting on the external format is not a reliable restructuring aid. Do not assume more tool moves substitute for a deliberate constraint-relaxation step.

finding: Motor movements did not help chunk decomposition (problem A) but interfered with relaxing higher-level constraints (operator constraint in B, tautology constraint in C). Authors say movement hurts when it does not match the cognitive demand.
numbers: Problem A: no movement effect. B (operator) and C (tautology): more movements went with lower success, reported as significant per problem; the pooled movement coefficient is near zero (-0.015 [-0.042,0.014]).
limits: Post hoc and correlational (movement count not assigned). The pooled null vs the per-problem effect is not fully reconciled in the text read.
agent_relevance: Low-level re-chunking and high-level constraint relaxation behave differently, so trigger type should match difficulty source. A stall trigger that only says 'try more moves' may hurt on constraint-type difficulty.

source: Graf et al. (2023) Tracing cognitive processes in insight problem solving: GAMs and change point analysis
finding: Eye tracking in matchstick arithmetic. ANOVA missed the abrupt shift; GAM and change-point (MCP) analyses located a sudden attention shift to the critical element (the plus sign) for solvers near the 90 percent bin of the solving period. An explicit hint given to non-solvers produced an immediate, qualitatively different jump in fixations.
numbers: Change point at about the 90 percent temporal bin for solvers; non-solvers shifted weakly. Exact N not re-extracted this session.
limits: MCP needs a priori number of change points (authors). Matchstick arithmetic only. N not re-read.
agent_relevance: The shift is late and abrupt, so a trigger based on gradual drift would not predict it. An external hint gives a different dynamic from a self-generated shift, matching the forced vs spontaneous contrast in d05.

source: Ormerod, Rusconi, Banks, MacGregor, Modelling insight: the case of the nine-dot problem (CogSci proceedings; year not printed in extracted text)
finding: Executable ACT-R model of CSP for the nine-dot problem. Stage 1: maximisation, picking the move that cancels most dots, checked against a criterion = remaining dots / remaining lines. Criterion failure triggers relaxation of the minimisation heuristic; stage 2 parses best moves for invariants and extends lines. Reproduces impasse, fixation and rare Aha.
numbers: 50 model runs: solution rate under 5 percent (humans under 5 percent). 13-dot variant solved within 2 runs; 12- and 11-dot variants within under 10 runs; first line inside the grid needs fewer runs than outside, p<.01 (matches MacGregor 2001 Exps 4-5).
quote: Relaxation of minimisation is triggered by criterion failure.
limits: Initial representation is hard-wired. Open question: should maximisation be optimal or satisficing. Authors say knowledge-rich RCT accounts 'may be overly elaborate' for this problem. This is not the PRODIGI paper.
agent_relevance: Concrete detector design for a stall trigger: criterion = remaining gap / remaining moves, taken from the problem statement. Failure of the best available move to beat it widens the representation. Fits a relative stall rule.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models, Table 5 (forced reconsideration by domain)
finding: The near-zero gain on crosswords and Rush Hour sits on a floor: base accuracy was already tiny for these small models. Forced reconsideration helped only where the model had headroom.
numbers: Paired Pass1 to Pass2. Xword N=83,200: 9.70 to 10.15 percent (+0.45pp; wins 5,380 vs 5,004). Math N=320,000: 32.21 to 40.62 percent (+8.41pp; 50,574 vs 23,500). Rush Hour N=320,000: 0.0233 to 0.0363 percent (+0.01pp; 100 vs 58).
quote: Do not carry the +8.41pp over to puzzle items. Re-run on items where the model sits mid-range before picking a gate.
limits: Small RL-tuned models: Qwen2.5-1.5B (1,000 GRPO steps) as primary; Qwen2.5-7B and Llama 3.1-8B at 500 steps. Eval sets 130 crossword (synthetic), 500 math, 500 Rush Hour boards. Only gate tested: Pass-1 sequence entropy (top 20 vs bottom 80 percent).
agent_relevance: Gap 5: no gate for puzzle domains can be judged from this paper, because there was no headroom. A stronger model at 20-60 percent base accuracy is needed.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026), entropy and domain mapping
finding: The authors label cryptic crosswords as representational change and math as progress monitoring. Link between entropy and spontaneous shifts differs by domain.
numbers: Odds ratio of a shift per standardised entropy: pooled 0.77 (beta -0.258, SE 0.143, p=.070, N=723,200); crosswords about 2.05; Rush Hour about 1.19; math about 0.58. Spontaneous shifts in math: high-entropy delta -7.40pp, low-entropy -22.88pp. Crosswords high-entropy delta +0.63pp (noisy).
limits: The domain-to-theory mapping is the authors' label. No condition varies tightness vs distance, so no RCT vs PM discrimination.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: token entropy is a usable stall proxy only per domain, since the sign flips between math and crosswords. A single entropy threshold is not safe.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles Reveal Limits of Machine Insight and Self-Evaluation
finding: Verification failure is described and counted, but no endorse step is tested. Authors only list better calibration, structured verification and stopping mechanisms as directions.
numbers: 38 frontier LLMs, zero-shot, retrieval-free. Verification failures are 5 to 39 percent of incorrect answers across models with usable thought logs. Human mean 52.9 percent; non-reasoning 7.6 percent and reasoning 17.6 percent on the 120-item human subset.
limits: Gap 7 stays open: nobody adds an explicit endorse step or measures its token cost. Thought-log coding is qualitative.
agent_relevance: Upper bound for an endorse step: the correct candidate was visible in 5-39 percent of wrong answers. Test as an A/B on NazoNazo-style items and count extra tokens.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025), contamination checks and release-date trend
finding: Contamination evidence is indirect. Items 1-159 are released only in hashed form. Three search-augmented models served as a probe and some came close to human scores, read by the authors as external text access. Release date correlates with accuracy; parameter size does not.
numbers: Release date vs accuracy Spearman .402, p=.0123 (n=38); size Pearson r=-0.017, p=.919 (n=38). Non-reasoning 9.42 percent vs reasoning 19.25 percent on all 201 items; Welch t(24.093)=2.976, p=.00655, d=0.946 (model level); item-level pooled OR 2.29 [1.99,2.64].
quote: Use hashed or freshly generated items when comparing triggers.
limits: No pre/post-cutoff item split, so contamination cannot be separated from real gains over time. Paper states RiddleSense is now often training data and that metacognitive prompting gives GPT-4 above 98 percent on BRAINTEASER.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 partly closed: classic English sets (candle, nine-dot, RAT, BRAINTEASER, RiddleSense) are contaminated or saturated; hashed Japanese riddles are the cleaner test. Per-item contamination is still unmeasured.

source: Orru et al. (2023) Human-like problem-solving abilities in large language models using ChatGPT
finding: ChatGPT on 30 classic verbal insight problems (15 practice, 15 transfer) with human solve rates from 20 subjects. Its score equalled the most probable human outcome and fell within the 5 percent most probable human outcomes.
numbers: 30 problems, 0/1 scoring, max 15 per set; human reference N=20.
limits: Reply text in the paper shows 'my training data goes until 2021'; items are widely published, so memorisation is not excluded. Human sample is small.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: plausible contamination case, in contrast to the roughly 35-point gap to humans on fresh Japanese riddles (d08).

source: Qiu, Zhou, Schooler (2026) The Cost of Coordination: Why Multi-Agent LLMs Explore More But Discover Less, CogSci 48
finding: On insight-type situation puzzles, two-agent GPT-4o teams were less accurate than solo agents. The cost splits into a protocol failure part (47 percent, fewer host-directed questions) and a residual convergence cost (53 percent). Doubling time kept the ratio.
numbers: N=82 sessions, 2 (solo/team) x 2 (time) design; mediation 47 percent / 53 percent; teams directed about 26-27 percent of the solo count of host-directed turns (paper's wording).
limits: One model (GPT-4o); an LLM host scores puzzles; question categories assigned by keyword rules.
agent_relevance: Unstructured divergent exploration did not give restructuring; convergence is the weak phase, consistent with d07. More parallel exploration is not a substitute for a convergence step.

source: Haq, Chhaya, Pandey, Bhattacharya (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Einstellung-style test on Llama-3.1-8B, 70B and GPT-4o. With chain-of-thought, solutions took more than one step where humans use one step, read as a CoT-induced shift of mental set.
numbers: Table 2 exact match for SP / SP+CPF / CP / CP+SPF: Llama-8B .50/.66/.33/.83; Llama-70B .50/.66/.66/.83; GPT-4o .66/.66/.83/.83; steps 3 in all cells. Values are multiples of 1/6.
limits: About 6 problems per cell, no statistics: anecdotal.
agent_relevance: Direction fits fixation by prior strategy, but cannot weigh an RCT trigger against a progress trigger. Low weight.

source: Korovkin, Vladimirov, Chistopolskaya, Savinova (2018) How working memory provides representational change during insight problem solving
finding: Dual-task probe RT: WM load rises across the solving period in both insight and non-insight problems, but insight problems load WM less than non-insight ones. Non-insight solving relates to the control system; insight solving recruits storage and control at different stages.
numbers: Experimental group 32 (25 women, M age 22.16), control 32 (22 women). Stage main effect and stage x task interaction significant. Stage-1 load similar in insight and non-insight problems and above baseline.
quote: insight problem solving is demanding in terms of working memory, non-insight problem solving is notably more so
limits: Probe RT is an indirect measure. Paper cites DeCaro 2016 second-hand: higher WM capacity goes with lower matchstick accuracy via inhibited constraint relaxation.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: supports a staged view (comprehension and search load WM; restructuring is brief and rare). Predicts that long context or wide branching hurts the search stage more than the reframe stage. Test: raise branching while holding the reframe fixed.

source: Chao, Hsieh, Wu (2025) Long-distance exploration in insightful problem-solving, Communications Psychology
finding: On Japanese remote-associates items, insight and Aha go with exploration across larger distances in the solution space; simulation shows de-fixation plus broad exploration. Aha is more frequent when fixation cues are closer (a strong impasse resolved).
numbers: n=349 and n=105 participants in two RAT versions; Aha vs fixation-cue distance beta -0.13 [-0.21,-0.05], t(2789)=-3.24, p=.0012.
limits: Verbal RAT only; authors say their model does not cover representational change.
agent_relevance: Supports a search-breadth operator (sample a far candidate) as a third trigger arm beside reframe and progress checks; not a test of the two theories.

source: Fedor, Zachar, Szilagyi, Ollinger, de Vladar, Szathmary (2017) Cognitive architecture with evolutionary dynamics solves insight problem
finding: A neural model (Darwinian Neurodynamics) solves the four-tree problem. Priming without pretraining gave the highest solve rate (beginner's luck effect); capacity and learning deficits lowered performance.
numbers: Three experiments; Exp1 matches the direction of Kershaw 2013 human priming data.
limits: One problem; no RCT vs progress contrast; abstract only read.
agent_relevance: Marginal for trigger choice. Shows an implemented candidate-population process with priming.

source: Nasvytis and Fan (2026) Leveraging speech to identify signatures of insight and transfer (re-read for frame transfer)
finding: Participants improved faster when the same problem type repeated, and time per problem fell. Frame discovery transfers to the same type, weakly to others.
numbers: N=189 analysed; time after first success 89.9 s (Same) vs 179.0 s (Different); Different-condition later accuracy 44.0 percent.
limits: Humans, matchstick arithmetic, five-problem sequence. No agent memory test.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open: a type-tag-keyed memory is the natural analogue, but no study compares it with untagged memory at equal tokens.

source: Jones (2003) Testing two cognitive theories of insight, JEP:LMC 29(5), 1017-1027 (fetch attempted)
finding: Could not be opened. The DOI redirects to PsycNet, which returned only a loading shell. Europe PMC lists the record as not open access. Per-cell table not obtained, so gap 2 stays open.
limits: K02 counts remain derived from sibling folder 04 and stay provisional.
agent_relevance: No change. Needs an institutional copy or author PDF.

source: Ormerod and MacGregor (2020) The complementary roles of knowledge and strategy in insight problem-solving (re-read intro)
finding: CSP offers no account of initial matchstick difficulty (scope and tightness act independently of perceived progress) but offers a discovery mechanism that does not need switching off knowledge. RCT must explain how unwanted knowledge is switched off and back on. Experiment 1 varies value size as a signal for most-progress moves.
numbers: No new numbers; design is loose/tight chunk x low/high value, standard and reverse tautology.
limits: Outcome table inconsistency (13/30 vs 11/29) not resolved.
agent_relevance: The two theories fit as complementary triggers: knowledge trigger for what to relax, progress trigger for when to search. Test them factorially.
